$comment: The server's own settings (apps/server/README.md), the same for every region it serves. What it keeps and derives from recordings is in recording.json; deployment settings that differ between environments are environment variables (apps/server/src/env.ts).
$port: The port it listens on when PORT isn't set (local runs; the production image sets PORT, infra/server.Dockerfile).
$dispatchCheckS: Live dispatch (apps/server/README.md#live-dispatch-and-previews): how often the leader checks the confirmed observations and disruptions (the database, or config/regions/<rail region>/{observations,disruptions} without one) for changes. Only changed inputs re-dispatch a date; client requests never do.
$dispatchWindowDays: Live dispatch covers service dates this many days either side of today; older and later dates come from build:dispatch.
$tripUpdatesHealth: When /healthz fails a feed's trip updates for answering with delays for almost none of the buses: the feed is empty or no longer matches the positions (apps/server/README.md#real-time-service). A feed can override any of these (feed.json → realtime.tripUpdatesHealth). Guesses, from recorded data: TransLink 75-85 % in service hours and 36-60 % at night (2026-10-01 to 10-11), 0 from 04:00 on 2026-10-12 for hours while polls kept succeeding; BC Transit's Kelowna feed 0 % of 1-7 buses around 00:20 and 04:50-05:20, with buses signed on to trips the feed has dropped or doesn't list yet, dipping below 20 % of 11 buses for 5 minutes at 05:18 (2026-10-19).

tripUpdatesHealth.$minCoverage: It fails below this share of the buses on a trip with a delay...
tripUpdatesHealth.$minBuses: ...judged only on positions polls with at least this many buses on a trip (with a handful, one bus is a large share)...
tripUpdatesHealth.$lowForS: ...once it has stayed low this long (single polls dip; real outages last hours).

$diskMaxUsed: When /healthz fails for the disk that holds var/ being fuller than this share. In production that's the VM's one disk, which also holds the database and the nightly dump while it's staged, and Postgres needs headroom (deployment/README.md#sizing): 25 of 96 GB were used on 2026-10-25, growing ~0.2 GB a day until older observed stop times move out (#129).
